all_crs: I need my laptop’s battery to comfortably last a full real‑world day of typical light work, school, and casual use so I don’t have to stay near a charger.

I want my laptop to have a modern, power-efficient CPU and integrated graphics that keep everyday work, web, video, and light gaming fast and smooth without overheating or slowing down, even on battery.
I want my laptop to be light and compact enough that I can carry it around throughout the day without it feeling heavy or bulky.
I want my laptop’s keyboard to be comfortable, accurate, and durable for long typing sessions, with a sensible layout, stable keys, well‑placed navigation, and effective backlighting where present.

I need my laptop to have a well-chosen, robust mix of common ports (e.g., USB-A, USB-C/Thunderbolt, HDMI/DP, audio, and sometimes Ethernet/SD) so I can connect typical peripherals and displays without relying on many dongles.
I want my laptop’s display to be bright, low-glare, and comfortable to view in typical and bright environments without distracting reflections or eye strain.
I want my laptop to have a 13–16 inch screen with a practical aspect ratio that balances comfortable workspace with portability.
I want my laptop’s RAM and storage to be user-upgradeable and not fully soldered so I can add capacity later as my needs grow.
I need my work laptop to be physically durable and robust (chassis, materials, components) so it survives many years of daily professional use and travel.
I want my professional laptop to have enough RAM (and support for ≥32 GB where needed) so I can run IDEs, many tabs, VMs, data tools, and creative apps smoothly.
I need my professional laptop to offer capable graphics (integrated or discrete) appropriate to my work, from smooth multi‑monitor and video calls to demanding 3D, CAD, or AI workloads.
I need my professional laptop’s cooling system to keep internal components cool and prevent thermal throttling or damage during sustained heavy workloads.
I want my professional laptop to be reasonably serviceable and modular (RAM, SSD, battery, fans, hinges, cooling) so it can be repaired and upgraded instead of replaced.
I need my professional laptop to include ample, fast internal storage and options for expansion (multiple slots, large SSDs) so I can keep big projects, VMs, and datasets locally.

I want my laptop’s integrated graphics to be capable enough to run light or older games (e.g., Minecraft, GTA V, Valorant, emulators) at modest settings and playable frame rates so I can casually game without a bulky gaming rig.
I want my casual‑use laptop to have enough RAM (typically at least 8–16 GB) so common multitasking with many browser tabs, streaming, and office apps stays smooth now and over several years.
I need enough internal storage, on a fast SSD, that my OS, apps, photos, and a few games fit comfortably and everyday use feels snappy.
I want my laptop’s casing materials and finishes to resist scratches, stains, fingerprints, and peeling feet or trim so it still looks and feels good after years of daily use.

I’d like my laptop’s design to be practical and understated—a traditional clamshell shape with normal rectangular screen and thin bezels, without flashy gamer styling or odd geometries that waste usable screen or feel out of place at work or class.
I want my laptop’s cooling system, vents, and dust resistance to work well on real‑world surfaces like desks, laps, beds, and kitchen tables without quickly clogging or needing a cooling pad.
